source: NASA SRTM 30 m (SRTMGL1 v003) via Open-Topo-Data
note: Ground elevation sampled at 100 to 200 points along each line, from NASA's Shuttle Radar Topography Mission 30 m model. Distances are along the path in kilometres; elevations are metres above sea level and can be negative, because parts of the Western Desert are. A null elevation means the model has no value at that point and is drawn as a gap, never as zero. SRTM measures the reflective surface, so buildings and dense vegetation sit slightly above bare ground. This is a measurement of the land, not a rendering of it, and no part of it is an artist's impression.

transects.name: Across the valley at Luxor
transects.why: West to east at the latitude of the Theban necropolis: desert, then the tomb valleys, then the floodplain, the river, Karnak, and desert again. The strip of green Egypt actually lives on is the flat part in the middle, and this is how wide it is.

transects.name: The Giza plateau edge
transects.why: East to west from the Nile floodplain, up the limestone scarp the pyramids stand on, and out into the Western Desert. The builders did not raise that ground; they chose it.

transects.name: From the Gulf of Aqaba up to Saint Catherine
transects.why: Dahab is at sea level and Saint Catherine's Monastery sits above 1500 m about eighty kilometres inland. This is the climb between them, and it is the reason the monastery is cold.

transects.name: Siwa and the depressions
transects.why: West of the Nile the desert is not flat. It falls below sea level — Siwa sits in one hollow and the Qattara Depression, the lowest land in Africa outside the Afar, is the next one north.

transects.name: The Nile, Cairo to Abu Simbel
transects.why: Following the river rather than a straight line, because a straight line from Cairo to Abu Simbel crosses the Eastern Desert and would read as a mountain range. About a thousand kilometres, and the ground barely rises: the median along this line is the floodplain, and the whole fall from Cairo to the First Cataract is less than the height of the Great Pyramid. The legs between waypoints are straight, so where the river meanders hardest the line clips the terrace above it and a few samples spike — those are real desert readings on a line that left the water, not errors, and the median below is the honest summary of the profile.
